evals.prompt: second order effects for my login defences page. phase2_fp.md is done and the rows are below with their grades. group second_order_thinking-workspace, slug eval_login_defences. the map has 3 domains. d1 login controls: d1a lockout after repeated failed logins (g5), d1b same error text for a bad user and a bad password (g4). d2 session cookie: d2a HttpOnly flag on the session cookie (g5), d2b idle timeout left at its default (g4). d3 bot checks: d3a CAPTCHA after repeated failures (g2), d3b what a CAPTCHA token proves (g4). fill the chain. which sections get a next-event sentence?
evals.expected_output: A filled phase2_so.md for eval_login_defences in the scratch group, with its path and the Pair sentence in the reply. A header with 3 domain sections, cap 1, at most one section with a next-event sentence, a review date and a reviewer. A chain table with the nine columns and bare node ids. d3a is a row with no: base. d3b is a definition: it sits in the No chain list, or in the table with no: reader. The other four nodes are traced to a second and third order. Each filled order cell ends with its grade. Horizon and who responds are filled (party: effect for each listed party that responds, or none). Lesson cells read yes or no with a reason. Any effect with no opened source is g2, not verified. Kept rows: none or one, and at least one section carries no sentence. A Stops block and a Review log. No HTML page. The reply is at most 150 words of prose plus the path. On substance: lockout turned into a denial of service, HttpOnly that does not stop session riding under XSS, and user enumeration that moves to other channels, each named as a later effect, sourced or marked g2.
assertions: [format] The reply carries the Pair sentence unchanged: 'Pair: first_principles wrote phase2_fp.md (what is true). second_order_thinking wrote phase2_so.md (what follows).' It names the path Artifacts/artifacts/second_order_thinking-workspace/eval_login_defences/phase2_so.md.

[format] The chain table has these nine headers in this order: node id, decision or mechanism, first order, second order, third order, horizon, who responds, lesson (yes or no, with the reason), grade. Each of d1a, d1b, d2a, d2b, d3a and d3b appears once, as a bare id with no braces, in the table or in the No chain list.

[format] The file states the cap as 1 (3 domain sections divided by 3, rounded down) and keeps at most one next-event sentence in total, unless it names an exception that cites a side effect and a source id. At least one section carries no sentence, even under an exception.
[format] Every lesson cell starts with yes or no and gives a reason. Every no reason names the failed test: reader, kind, source, cap or base.
[format] d3a gets no chain: its lesson cell says no with base as the reason, because its base grade g2 is below g3.

[format] Every filled order cell ends with its grade in the form (g4). Every grade cell holds one digit from 1 to 5. An effect with no opened source ends with (g2, not verified). No effect carries a percentage or a probability without a source id.

[format] Every who responds cell names only the listed system parties (users, operators, attackers, vendors), gives each named party an effect, leaves out a party that does not respond, and uses the word none only where no listed party responds.
[format] The reply prose is at most 150 words, not counting the path and the Pair sentence. The chain table stays in the file.

[substance] The chain for d1a names lockout used as a denial of service against real users (an attacker locks an account on purpose) as a later effect. If d1a is kept as the one next-event sentence, its lesson cell cites an opened source at g3 or higher. With no opened source the effect ends (g2, not verified) and d1a is not kept.

[substance] The chain for d2a, or its lesson cell, names that HttpOnly does not stop a script that runs in the page from acting as the logged-in user (session riding under XSS), as a later effect or as a condition.

[substance] The chain for d1b names that the same error text does not by itself stop user enumeration: the leak can move to other channels such as response time or a reset or sign-up form. The effect is sourced, or it ends (g2, not verified).

evals.prompt: and then what? i want one conditional access policy that requires MFA and blocks legacy auth for every user in the tenant, emergency accounts included, because it is simpler. no map for this one, just the decision. think it through. group second_order_thinking-workspace, slug eval_ca_mfa.
evals.expected_output: A one-row chain for chat1, written to Artifacts/artifacts/second_order_thinking-workspace/eval_ca_mfa/phase2_so.md. The Pair sentence in its chat-only form. First, second and third order filled in that one row, each ending with its grade, with a horizon on the 10 min, 10 mo, 10 yr scale. Side effects sit inside the order cells, not in extra rows. Who responds uses only the listed system parties (users, operators, attackers, vendors), with an effect for each party named, and leaves out a party that does not respond. The exception names the topic as a decision. Unsourced effects are g2, not verified. A later effect where the policy locks out the people who must fix an outage is the kind to look for. It stays g2 unless a source was opened. The reply names the later effect that matters most and says it is a guess. A review date, a reviewer and a stop reason are in the file. The reply is at most 150 words of prose plus the path.
assertions: [format] The Pair sentence is the chat-only form: 'Pair: first_principles not run (chat-only decision). second_order_thinking wrote phase2_so.md (what follows).' The reply names the path Artifacts/artifacts/second_order_thinking-workspace/eval_ca_mfa/phase2_so.md.

[format] The Chain table has exactly one row, with the bare id chat1, and no other node id in the table. The No chain list says none. Side effects sit inside its order cells. The first, second and third order cells are all filled, and each ends with a grade. The horizon cell uses 10 min, 10 mo or 10 yr.

[format] The who responds cell names only the listed system parties (users, operators, attackers, vendors), gives each named party an effect, leaves out a party that does not respond, and uses the word none only if no listed party responds.
[format] The lesson cell starts with yes or no and gives a reason. The header names an exception because the topic is itself a decision, so no cap number is applied.
[format] Every effect with no opened source ends with (g2, not verified). No effect carries a percentage, a count or a probability without a source id.

[format] The header shows a review date in YYYY-MM-DD form and a reviewer. The Stops block gives a reason for the order where the chain stops: the next order would not change the decision, is below the noise, or three orders are done.
[format] The reply prose is at most 150 words, not counting the path and the Pair sentence. It names the later effect that matters most and says it is a guess when no source was opened.

[substance] A later effect names that the emergency (break-glass) accounts, kept under a policy that requires MFA, can be locked out when the MFA service or the identity provider fails, so nobody can repair the policy. The effect is sourced, or it ends (g2, not verified).

[substance] A later effect names that accounts and clients that cannot answer an MFA prompt (service accounts, automation, legacy clients) stop working under the policy. The effect is sourced, or it ends (g2, not verified).
